The term "parthenocarpy" means the development of the ovary into a fruit without fertilisation.
Complete the statement: Oogenesis takes place in the follicle of the _____.
Oogenesis takes place in the follicle of the ovary.
Complete the statement: The spores of Rhizopus are small, light and _____.
The spores of Rhizopus are small, light and dry.
Complete the statement: The _____ is the part of the stamen that contains the pollen sacs.
The anther is the part of the stamen that contains the pollen sacs.
Complete the statement: The term "_____" means a triploid (3n) tissue formed when the second sperm fuses with the fusion nucleus.
The term "endosperm" means a triploid (3n) tissue formed when the second sperm fuses with the fusion nucleus.
What is the framework of hard structures that gives physical support and protection to the body of an animal called?
The framework of hard structures that provides physical support and protection for the bodies of animals is called the skeleton.
What do we call a skeleton that lies inside the body, as in humans and other vertebrates?
Like that of other vertebrates, the human skeleton lies inside the body and is therefore an endoskeleton.
What is a skeleton present outside the body, as in some invertebrates, called?
The skeleton of some invertebrates is outside the body and is called an exoskeleton.
Which group of invertebrates is given in the chapter as an example of animals with an exoskeleton?
The skeletal system of some invertebrates, for example arthropods, is outside the body.
The human skeleton is made of which kind of tissue?
The human skeleton is made of living tissue.
Besides living cells and nerves, what else does the skeleton contain?
The skeleton contains living cells, nerves and blood vessels.
Apart from growing, what does the living skeleton do to itself after an injury?
The living skeleton can grow and repair itself after an injury.
To what does the dynamic living skeleton adapt?
The skeleton is a living tissue that can grow, repair itself after injury and adapt to stress.
What is another name for the free movement of animals?
Free movement, also known as locomotion, is a life characteristic of all living animals.
From whom does locomotion help animals to save themselves?
Locomotion enables animals to utilise the environment in the best possible way and to save themselves from predators.
Which common invertebrate found in the soil always crawls and moves slowly because it has no skeleton?
The earthworm always crawls on the ground and moves slowly because it does not have any skeleton.
Which structure is missing in an earthworm, so that it cannot stand erect or move faster?
An earthworm cannot stand erect and move faster because it does not have any skeleton to support it.
What does the hard structure of the skeleton give to the body?
The skeleton forms the hard structure of the body and gives it a definite shape.
Which tissues attached to the bones make the bones move, so that we can move?
Skeletal muscles are attached to the bones, so the bones can move and thus we can move.
Which organ is protected by the skull?
Which structure is protected by the vertebral column?
The vertebral column protects the spinal cord.
Which part of the skeleton protects the heart and lungs?
The lungs and heart are protected in the rib cage.
Which part of the skeleton produces red blood cells, platelets and white blood cells?
The bone marrow produces red blood cells, platelets and white blood cells.
Bone marrow produces red blood cells, white blood cells and which other blood component?
Bone marrow produces red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets.
Which mineral salt, stored in bones, keeps them hard and strong?
Bones store mineral salts such as potassium, phosphorus and calcium.
Along with calcium and potassium, which mineral salt is stored in bones?
Bones store the mineral salts calcium, potassium and phosphorus.
Along with calcium and phosphorus, which mineral salt is stored in bones?
Bones store the mineral salts calcium, phosphorus and potassium.
Which kind of substances stored in bones keep them hard and strong?
Bones remain hard and strong because they store mineral salts.
In different animals, the shape of the skeleton is in accordance with which aspect of the particular animal's type?
In different animals, the shape of the skeleton is in accordance with the requirement of the particular animal's type.
Shape, support, movement, protection and which other function are performed by the skeleton in the living body?
The functions of the skeleton include shape, support, movement, protection and blood cells production.
Into how many main parts is the human skeleton divided?
The human skeleton is composed of two parts: the axial skeleton and the appendicular skeleton.
The human skeleton consists of the axial skeleton and which other part?
The human skeleton consists of the axial skeleton and the appendicular skeleton.
How many bones does the axial skeleton consist of?
The axial skeleton consists of 80 bones of the head, neck and chest.
How many bones does the appendicular skeleton consist of?
The appendicular skeleton consists of 126 bones of the limbs and the pectoral and pelvic girdles.
How many bones are present in an adult human skeleton?
An adult human skeleton has 206 bones.
The axial skeleton has the bones of the head, neck and which other body region?
The axial skeleton consists of 80 bones of the head, neck and chest.
The appendicular skeleton consists of the bones of the girdles and which other body parts?
The appendicular skeleton consists of 126 bones of the limbs and the pectoral and pelvic girdles.
Which word describes the point meant by the term "axis", around which other structures are distributed?
The term axis means the central point around which other structures are distributed.
In which part of the body does the axial skeleton lie?
The axial skeleton lies in the centre of the body, around which the whole body is built.
Which bone, along with the skull, vertebral column and ribs, forms the axial skeleton?
The axial skeleton includes the skull, the vertebral column, the ribs and the sternum.
The skull is made up of the facial bones and which other part?
The skull is made up of the cranium and the facial bones.
How many bones does the cranium consist of?
The cranium consists of 8 bones, which protect the brain.
Which organ is protected by the bones of the cranium?
The cranium consists of 8 bones, which protect the brain.
How many facial bones are there?
There are 14 facial bones, which make the skeletal part of our face.
Which bones make the skeletal part of our face?
The facial bones make the skeletal part of our face.
How many bones are there in the whole skull (cranium and facial bones together)?
The skull has 22 bones in all: 8 in the cranium and 14 facial bones.
The vertebral column extends from the skull to which structure?
The vertebral column extends from the skull to the pelvis.
Which structure of the axial skeleton allows us to stand erect?
The vertebral column allows us to stand erect and also protects the spinal cord.
How many vertebrae does the vertebral column consist of?
The vertebral column consists of 33 vertebrae.
How many cervical vertebrae are present in the neck?
There are 7 cervical vertebrae in the neck.
What are the vertebrae present in the neck called?
The vertebrae present in the neck are called cervical vertebrae.
How many thoracic vertebrae lie in the chest region?
There are 12 thoracic vertebrae in the chest region.
What are the vertebrae that lie in the chest region called?
The vertebrae which lie in the chest region are called thoracic vertebrae.
How many lumbar vertebrae lie in the back region?
There are 5 lumbar vertebrae in the back region.
What are the five vertebrae of the back region called?
The five vertebrae which lie in the back region are called lumbar vertebrae.
How many pelvic vertebrae are found between the lower limbs?
There are 9 pelvic vertebrae between the lower limbs.
The pelvic vertebrae form two sets. One is the sacrum; which is the other?
The pelvic vertebrae make two sets, the sacrum and the coccyx.
The sacrum is formed by the fusion of how many anterior vertebrae?
The sacrum is formed by the fusion of the anterior five vertebrae.
The coccyx is formed by the fusion of how many posterior vertebrae?
The coccyx is formed by the fusion of four posterior vertebrae.
Which part of the pelvic vertebrae is formed by the fusion of the anterior five vertebrae?
The sacrum is formed by the fusion of the anterior five vertebrae.
Which part of the pelvic vertebrae is formed by the fusion of four posterior vertebrae?
The coccyx is formed by the fusion of four posterior vertebrae.
How many pairs of ribs are present in the human body?
There are 12 pairs of ribs in the human body.
On which side are the ribs attached to the vertebrae?
The ribs are attached on the dorsal (back) side with the vertebrae.
How many pairs of ribs connect anteriorly with the sternum, either directly or through an arch?
Out of the 12 pairs of ribs, 10 pairs connect anteriorly with the chest bone (sternum).
Which bone is also called the chest bone?
The sternum is also called the chest bone.
The rib cage supports which cavity of the body, in which the heart and lungs lie?
The rib cage supports the thoracic cavity, in which vital organs like the heart and lungs lie.
How many of the lowest pairs of ribs are called floating ribs?
The lower 2 pairs of ribs are called floating ribs.
The lower 2 pairs of ribs are called floating ribs because they do not attach to which bone?
The lower 2 pairs of ribs are called floating ribs because they do not attach to the sternum.
How many small bones called ossicles are there in each human ear?
Each human ear has 3 bones called ossicles.
Which ear ossicle is named along with the incus and the stapes?
The three ossicles of the ear are the malleus, the incus and the stapes.
Which ear ossicle is named along with the malleus and the stapes?
The three ossicles of the ear are the malleus, the incus and the stapes.
Which ear ossicle is named along with the malleus and the incus?
The three ossicles of the ear are the malleus, the incus and the stapes.
What is the single bone in the neck called?
There is one bone in the neck called the hyoid bone.
About how many bones do human infants have at the time of birth?
At the time of birth human infants have 350 bones in their body.
What happens to many bones as a baby grows towards the adult stage, reducing their number to 206?
As a baby grows, many of the 350 bones fuse together and their number reduces to 206.
Which is the largest bone of the human body?
The largest bone of the human body is the femur.
Where is the smallest bone of the human body found?
The smallest bone of the human body is found in the internal ear.
Which skeleton includes the pectoral girdle, the pelvic girdle and the limbs (appendages)?
The appendicular skeleton consists of the pectoral girdle, the pelvic girdle and the limbs (appendages).
Which skeleton includes the skull, the vertebral column and the ribs with the sternum?
The axial skeleton includes the skull, the vertebral column and the ribs with the sternum.
Which girdle attaches the forelimbs to the vertebral column?
The pectoral girdle attaches the forelimbs to the vertebral column.
Which girdle attaches the hind limbs to the vertebral column?
The pelvic girdle attaches the hind limbs to the vertebral column.
The bones of the shoulder form which girdle?
The bones of the shoulder make up the pectoral girdle.
To which structure do the pectoral and pelvic girdles attach the limbs?
The pectoral and pelvic girdles attach the limbs to the vertebral column.
How many bones make up the pectoral girdle?
The pectoral girdle is comprised of 4 bones of the shoulder.
How many bones of the shoulder are there on each side in the pectoral girdle?
The pectoral girdle has 2 bones of the shoulder on each side.
How many bones does the pelvic girdle consist of?
The pelvic girdle consists of 2 bones.
How many bones are there in the two arms together?
The arms contain 6 bones (3 in each arm).
How many bones are there in each arm?
The arms contain 6 bones, with 3 bones in each arm.
How many bones are there in the two hands together?
The hands contain 54 bones (27 in each hand).
How many bones are there in each hand?
The hands contain 54 bones, with 27 bones in each hand.
How many bones are there in the two legs together?
The legs contain 8 bones (4 in each leg).
How many bones are there in each leg?
The legs contain 8 bones, with 4 bones in each leg.
How many bones are there in the two feet together?
The feet contain 52 bones (26 in each foot).
How many bones are there in each foot?
The feet contain 52 bones, with 26 bones in each foot.
What are the arms and hands together called in the appendicular skeleton?
In the appendicular skeleton, the arms and hands are called the forelimbs.
What are the legs and feet together called in the appendicular skeleton?
In the appendicular skeleton, the legs and feet are called the hind limbs.
Bones and which other tissue are the two types of connective tissue that make up the human skeleton?
The human skeleton is made up of two types of connective tissue: bones and cartilage.
Bones and cartilage are two types of which kind of tissue?
Bones and cartilage are the two types of connective tissue that make up the human skeleton.
Which is the hardest and most rigid form of connective tissue in the human body?
Bone is the hardest and most rigid form of connective tissue in the human body.
Bones give shape and which other quality to the body, while protecting delicate internal organs?
Bones give shape and structure to the body and protect delicate internal organs.
What is the hard, white outer layer of a bone called?
The hard, white outer layer of a bone is called compact bone.
Which protein fibres are present in the matrix of bone?
The matrix of compact bone contains collagen fibres and is saturated with calcium phosphate.
Which compound saturates the bone matrix and gives strength to the bone?
The matrix of bone is saturated with calcium phosphate, which gives strength to the bone.
In which spaces do the bone cells called osteocytes lie?
Bone cells called osteocytes lie in spaces called lacunae.
Which structures in the bone matrix keep the osteocytes alive?
The bone matrix contains nerve fibres and blood vessels that keep the osteocytes alive.
Which type of bone lies beneath the compact bone?
Beneath the compact bone is the spongy bone.
What do the spaces of the spongy bone contain?
The spaces of the spongy bone contain bone marrow, where most blood cells are formed.
In the spaces of which bone layer is the bone marrow found?
Bone marrow is found in the spaces of the spongy bone.
Which specialised connective tissue is firm and flexible and does not stretch?
Cartilage is a specialised connective tissue which is firm and flexible and does not stretch.
Which kind of strength does cartilage have in a great amount?
Compared with bone, how is cartilage?
Cartilage is much softer than bone.
In adults, where does cartilage cover the ends of the bones?
In adults, cartilage covers the ends of bones at joints.
Cartilage supports the flexible portion of the nose and which part of the external ear?
Cartilage supports the flexible portion of the nose and the external ears (pinna).
How is the ground substance of cartilage described?
The ground substance of cartilage is an amorphous gel-like substance.
Which protein fibres are present in the ground substance of cartilage in parallel arrangements?
The ground substance of cartilage contains collagen fibres in parallel arrangements.
What are the cells of cartilage called?
The cells of cartilage are called chondrocytes.
In which spaces do the cartilage cells called chondrocytes lie?
The cells of cartilage, the chondrocytes, lie in spaces called lacunae.
What about the chondrocytes found in cartilage determines how flexible or elastic the cartilage is?
The number of chondrocytes found in cartilage determines how flexible or elastic the cartilage is.
What is absent in the ground substance of cartilage?
There are no blood vessels in the ground substance of cartilage.
Cartilage keeps bones from rubbing together, thus reducing what?
One of the main functions of cartilage is to keep bones from rubbing together, thus reducing friction.
What is cartilage called in common words?
In common words, cartilage is referred to as "soft bone".
Of what is the whole skeleton made in early embryonic life?
In early embryonic life the whole skeleton is made of cartilage.
Into what does the cartilage of the embryonic skeleton gradually turn?
In early embryonic life the whole skeleton is made of cartilage, which then gradually turns into bones.
How many types of cartilage are there?
There are three types of cartilage: elastic, hyaline and fibrous.
Which type of cartilage has cells closer together with less ground substance?
Elastic cartilage has cells closer together with less ground substance.
Which type of cartilage, found at the ends of long bones, has fewer cells and more ground substance?
Hyaline cartilage, found at the ends of long bones, has fewer cells and more ground substance.
Which type of cartilage has the least number of cells and therefore the maximum ground substance?
Fibrous cartilage has the least number of cells and so the maximum ground substance.
Elastic cartilage is found in the external ear flaps and which structure of the throat?
Elastic cartilage is found in the external ear flaps and the epiglottis.
Elastic cartilage is found in the epiglottis and which other structure?
Elastic cartilage is found in the epiglottis and the external ear flaps.
Hyaline cartilage is found at the ends of which bones?
Hyaline cartilage is found at the ends of long bones.
Hyaline cartilage is found in the nose, ears, larynx, bronchi and which tube?
Hyaline cartilage is found in the nose, ears, trachea, larynx and bronchi.
Hyaline cartilage is found in the trachea, larynx and which air tubes of the lungs?
Hyaline cartilage is found in the nose, ears, trachea, larynx and bronchi.
Fibrous cartilage is found in the inter-vertebral disc.
Which type of cartilage is found in the inter-vertebral disc?
The cartilage found in the inter-vertebral disc is fibrous cartilage.
A joint is formed at the meeting point of how many or more bones?
A joint is formed at the meeting point of two or more bones.
Joints keep the bones together, allow them to move to different extents and give what to the body?
Joints keep our bones together, allow the bones to move to different extents and give mobility to the body.
Joints are classified into three categories on the basis of the extent of what that they allow?
Joints are classified into three categories on the basis of the extent of movement they allow.
Into how many categories are joints classified on the basis of the movement they allow?
On the basis of the extent of movement they allow, joints are classified into three categories.
In which type of joints are the bones fused together, allowing no movement?
In immovable joints, the bones are fused together and do not allow any movement.
Which type of joints are present among the bones of the skull?
The joints present among the bones of the skull are immovable joints.
Which type of joints allow only little movement?
Slightly movable joints allow little movement.
Which type of joints are the joints of the vertebral column and the ribs?
The joints of the vertebral column and the ribs are slightly movable joints.
Which type of joints allow free movements?
Freely movable joints allow free movements.
How many major types of freely movable joints are there?
There are two major types of freely movable joints: the hinge joint and the ball-and-socket joint.
Which freely movable joint allows movement only in two directions?
A hinge joint allows movement only in two directions.
In how many directions do hinge joints allow movement?
Hinge joints allow movement only in two directions.
Which freely movable joint allows movement in all directions (up, down, forward and backward)?
A ball-and-socket joint allows movement in all directions (up, down, forward and backward).
Which two joints of the body are hinge joints?
Hinge joints are present at the elbow and knee.
Which hinge joint is present in the arm, along with the knee in the leg?
Hinge joints are present at the knee and the elbow.
Which hinge joint is present in the leg, along with the elbow in the arm?
Hinge joints are present at the elbow and the knee.
Which two joints are examples of ball-and-socket joints?
The hip joint and shoulder joint are examples of ball-and-socket joints.
Which ball-and-socket joint is present in the shoulder, along with the hip joint?
The hip joint and the shoulder joint are examples of ball-and-socket joints.
Which ball-and-socket joint is present at the hip, along with the shoulder joint?
The hip joint and the shoulder joint are examples of ball-and-socket joints.
Which type of joint is the elbow?
The elbow is a hinge joint.
Which type of joint is the hip?
The hip is a ball-and-socket joint.
Which tough bands of connective tissue hold the bones at the joints in place?
Ligaments are tough bands of connective tissue which hold the bones at the joints in place.
Which tough connective tissues attach muscles to bones?
Tendons are tough connective tissues which attach muscles to bones.
A ligament connects which two structures?
A ligament connects bone to bone, while a tendon connects muscle to bone.
A tendon connects which two structures?
A tendon connects muscle to bone, while a ligament connects bone to bone.
Which tissue exerts a pulling force on the attached bone when a muscle contracts?
When a muscle contracts, the tendon exerts a pulling force on the attached bone.
Skeletal muscles are attached to bones by tough connective tissue called what?
Skeletal muscles are attached to bones by tough connective tissue called tendons.
Who wrote the first major book on human anatomy in 1543?
Andreas Vesalius wrote the first major book on human anatomy in 1543.
In which city was Andreas Vesalius born?
Andreas Vesalius was born in Brussels.
Vesalius was a professor of Anatomy at which university in Italy?
Vesalius was a professor of Anatomy at Padua University in Italy.
In which country is the Padua University where Vesalius was a professor?
Padua University, where Vesalius was a professor, is in Italy.
Of which subject was Vesalius a professor at Padua University?
Vesalius was a professor of anatomy at Padua University in Italy.
In which year did Vesalius write the first major book on human anatomy?
In 1543 Vesalius wrote the first major book on human anatomy.
In which year was Andreas Vesalius born?
Andreas Vesalius (1514–1564) was born in Brussels.
In which year did Andreas Vesalius die?
Andreas Vesalius (1514–1564) was a professor of Anatomy at Padua University.
What is the English title of the first major book on human anatomy written by Vesalius in 1543?
The Fabric of the Human Body
The Map of the Human Body
In 1543 Vesalius wrote the first major book on human anatomy, called "The Fabric of the Human Body".
Which famous artist produced the anatomical illustrations for the book of Vesalius?
Vesalius worked closely with the famous artist Titian, who produced anatomical illustrations for his book.
How many anatomical illustrations did Titian produce for the book of Vesalius?
The famous artist Titian produced 277 anatomical illustrations for the book of Vesalius.
Vesalius explained the different parts of the human skeleton, including the number of what?
Vesalius explained the different parts of the human skeleton, including the number of bones.
Besides the skeleton, the source and position of what did Vesalius describe, along with their functions?
Vesalius described the source and position of the muscles and provided information on their respective functions.
The first major book written by Vesalius in 1543 was on which subject?
In 1543 Vesalius wrote the first major book on human anatomy.
Locomotion and all other types of movement are due to which action of muscles?
Locomotion and all other types of movement are due to the contraction of muscles.
How many types of muscles are there in the body?
There are three types of muscles in the body: cardiac, smooth and skeletal.
Which type of muscle is also called heart muscle?
Cardiac muscle is also called heart muscle.
Cardiac muscle is what kind of muscle, since we cannot control its function?
Cardiac muscle is an involuntary muscle: we cannot control its function.
Which muscle keeps on contracting throughout life to pump blood?
Cardiac muscle keeps on contracting throughout life.
Contractions of cardiac muscle help the heart to do what with blood throughout the body?
The contractions of cardiac muscle help the heart pump blood throughout the body.
Which muscles are found in the walls of organs such as the digestive tract, blood vessels and urinary bladder?
Smooth muscles are found in the walls of organs such as the digestive tract, air passageways, blood vessels and the urinary bladder.
What do the contractions of smooth muscles move within the organs?
The contractions of smooth muscles move materials within the organs.
Which muscles are attached to the bones of the skeleton?
Skeletal muscles are attached to the bones of the skeleton.
Skeletal muscle contractions help us in movement and what else?
The contractions of skeletal muscles help us in movement and locomotion.
Which muscles are under voluntary control?
Skeletal muscles are under voluntary control.
One end of a skeletal muscle is always attached to which kind of bone?
One end of a skeletal muscle is always attached to a fixed bone and the other to a moving bone.
The other end of a skeletal muscle is always attached to which kind of bone?
One end of a skeletal muscle is always attached to a fixed bone and the other to a moving bone.
What is the point where a muscle attaches to the fixed bone called?
The point where the muscle attaches to the fixed bone is called the origin.
What is the point where a muscle attaches to the moving bone called?
The point where the muscle attaches to the moving bone is called the insertion.
In what arrangement are most skeletal muscles found?
Most skeletal muscles are arranged in pairs.
When one muscle of a pair contracts (pulls), what does the other muscle do?
When one muscle contracts (pulls), the other relaxes or elongates.
What is the phenomenon in which one muscle opposes the action of the other called?
The phenomenon in which one muscle opposes the action of the other is called antagonism.
What are muscles that oppose the action of each other called?
Muscles which oppose the action of each other are called antagonistic muscles.
Muscles can only do what to bones?
Muscles can only pull bones; they cannot push them.
The human body has over how many muscles responsible for all types of movement?
The human body has over 500 muscles responsible for all types of movement.
When one muscle of the pair contracts (shortens), the coordinated movement with its partner is known as what kind of movement?
When one muscle of a pair contracts (shortens) and the other relaxes, the coordinated movement is known as the antagonistic movement of muscles.
What happens to the length of a muscle when it contracts?
When a muscle contracts, it shortens.
What happens to the length of a muscle when it relaxes?
When one muscle of a pair contracts (shortens), the other relaxes (elongates).
Which muscle of the upper arm contracts to bend the lower arm upward?
The biceps contracts to move the lower arm up (flexion).
Which muscle of the upper arm contracts to straighten the lower arm?
The triceps contracts to straighten the lower arm (extension).
When the biceps contracts, its insertion pulls which bone upward?
When the biceps contracts, its insertion pulls the radius bone upward.
When the triceps contracts, its insertion pulls which bone back?
When the triceps contracts, its insertion pulls the ulna bone back.
What is the movement called in which the biceps contracts and the lower arm moves up?
When the biceps contracts and the lower arm moves up, the movement is called flexion.
What is the movement called in which the triceps contracts and the lower arm straightens?
When the triceps contracts and the lower arm straightens, the movement is called extension.
Since its contraction bends the lower arm, the biceps is known as which kind of muscle?
The biceps is the flexor of the lower arm.
Since its contraction straightens the lower arm, the triceps is known as which kind of muscle?
The triceps is the extensor of the lower arm.
When the biceps contracts, what does the triceps do?
When the biceps contracts, the triceps relaxes.
When the triceps contracts, what does the biceps do?
When the triceps contracts, the biceps relaxes.
In which state is the lower arm when it is bent?
When the lower arm is bent it is in the flexed state.
In which state is the lower arm when it hangs down?
When the lower arm hangs down it is in the extended state.
Which portion of many bones produces red blood cells, platelets and white blood cells?
The internal portion of many bones produces red blood cells, platelets and white blood cells.
Muscles pull our bones to enable what?
Muscles pull our bones to enable movements.
Bones give shape and structure to the body and protect which kind of internal organs?
Bones give shape and structure to the body and protect delicate internal organs.
Cartilage is firm and flexible but does not do what?
Cartilage is a specialised connective tissue which is firm and flexible and does not stretch.
What is another name for the vertebral column?
The vertebral column, also called the backbone, extends from the skull to the pelvis.
In an antagonistic pair, one muscle moves a bone in one direction. In which direction does the other muscle move it?
One muscle moves a bone in one direction while the other moves it in the opposite direction.
In which organ is cardiac muscle found?
Cardiac muscle is found in the heart.
Which type of joint is the knee?
The knee is a hinge joint.
Which type of joint is the shoulder?
The shoulder is a ball-and-socket joint.
During a cricket match, which tissue of a fast bowler may get pulled?
During a cricket match, the muscle of a fast bowler may get pulled.
Which part of a wrestler may get dislocated?
The joint of a wrestler may get dislocated.
What may get fractured in an accident?
In an accident, the bones of a person may be fractured.
Which process forms bones by depositing calcium phosphate in the collagen fibres?
The process of mineralisation forms bones: calcium phosphate is deposited in the collagen fibres to make the bones hard.
In mineralisation, which compound is deposited in the collagen fibres to make the bones hard?
In mineralisation, calcium phosphate is deposited in the collagen fibres to make the bones hard.
In mineralisation, calcium phosphate is deposited in which fibres?
In mineralisation, calcium phosphate is deposited in the collagen fibres to make the bones hard.
From where is the calcium needed by the bones absorbed?
The calcium needed by the bones is absorbed from the food we eat.
When a person does not take sufficient calcium in the daily diet, the bones start becoming what?
When a person is not taking sufficient calcium in their daily diet, their bones start becoming weak.
What is the process called in which calcium moves from the bones to the blood?
The process in which calcium moves from the bones to the blood is called demineralisation.
In demineralisation, calcium moves from the bones to which fluid?
In demineralisation, calcium moves from the bones to the blood.
Calcium moves from the bones to the blood in demineralisation to maintain what in the blood?
Calcium moves from the bones to the blood in order to maintain the calcium level of the blood.
If demineralisation continues for a long time, the bones become what?
If this situation prolongs, the bones become soft and fragile.
What is the disorder in which the bones become soft and fragile called?
The disorder in which the bones become soft and fragile is known as osteoporosis.
Osteoporosis occurs especially in old people and in whom?
Osteoporosis occurs especially in old people and in women.
In osteoporosis, the bones start doing what and can be broken easily?
In osteoporosis the bones start bending and can be broken easily.
A prolonged deficiency of which mineral in the diet leads to osteoporosis?
A prolonged deficiency of calcium in the diet leads to osteoporosis.
Which disorder is the inflammation of the joints?
Arthritis is the disorder of the joints in which they get inflamed.
Arthritis is which kind of disease that damages the joints permanently?
Arthritis is a degenerative disease that damages the joints permanently.
Arthritis damages the joints permanently, causing which three symptoms?
Arthritis damages the joints permanently, causing pain, stiffness and swelling.
In arthritis, what do the membranes lining the joints do?
In arthritis the membranes lining the joints thicken and fluid production decreases.
In arthritis, what happens to the production of fluid in the joints?
In arthritis the membranes lining the joints thicken and fluid production decreases, which increases friction.
In later stages, arthritis leads to complete what?
In later stages arthritis leads to complete immobility, and the joints become permanently swollen and de-shaped.
How many types of arthritis are described in the chapter?
There are three types of arthritis: osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis and gouty arthritis.
Which is the most common type of arthritis?
Osteoarthritis is the most common type of arthritis.
Which tissue starts to wear away over time in osteoarthritis?
In osteoarthritis the cartilage starts to wear away over time.
